headline: Meta launches Muse Wonder, its first frontier AI model
dek: Wonder and Wonder Full ship through the API and Muse Code, and Meta says they match rivals (Meta, TechCrunch, The Verge).

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Meta's first frontier release
body: Meta announced on Monday Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, the first frontier models from Meta Superintelligence Labs (Meta Newsroom, TechCrunch, The Verge).
Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and to Muse Code subscribers. Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code subscribers and is not served through the API (TechCrunch).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Memory, focus and guardrails
s3.body: Meta says the models target agentic tasks, where an AI carries out multi-step work for the user (Meta Newsroom).

points.t: Keeps details relevant to an ongoing task across separate conversations, such as a lease review (Meta Newsroom).
Lets a model try different approaches on a hard task and recover from errors without losing the goal (Meta Newsroom).
Trained to ask confirmation before important actions and refuse harmful requests (Meta Newsroom).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A benchmark claim against rivals
body: Meta claims, in internal tests from its model card, that the models score comparably to GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (TechCrunch, The Verge).
Pricing is roughly in line with GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5, per TechCrunch. The Verge says the comparison with Google's Gemini 4 Argon is still unclear.

items.t: Both models will power Meta's Muse AI agent, rolling out first to subscribers (Meta Newsroom, TechCrunch, The Verge).
Meta says a fuller safety report with additional evaluations will be published soon (Meta Newsroom).
Wonder Full is not served through the API, and no change was announced (TechCrunch).

caption.hook: Meta launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, the first frontier models from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
body: TechCrunch notes this is the first frontier-level release since Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang restructured Meta's AI efforts in August of last year. The models follow Muse Spark, which Meta describes as a lightweight model built for low latency.

Research scientist Kavya Kopparapu told TechCrunch the team put effort into making sure the model can remember what matters to a user over days, weeks and months. According to TechCrunch, training took place at Meta's Prometheus data center in Ohio.
Meta says developers can also use Wonder to find flaws in their code.
caption.cta: Which long-running tasks would most benefit from a model that remembers across sessions?
